title: Quadratics & Nonlinear Equations
sub: 20 SPRs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Official Digital SAT Curriculum

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $\sqrt{2x+1}=5$, what is $x$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $12$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $2x+1=25 \Rightarrow x=12$. Therefore, the verified correct option is 12.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: In the plane, a parabola is given by $f(x) = 3(x - 4)^2 + 11$. What is the vertical intercept $f(0)$?

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^2+x-7$, what is $f(6)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $71$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(6)=2(6)^2+1(6)-7=71$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 71.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^2+2x-3$, what is $f(2)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $9$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(2)=2(2)^2+2(2)-3=9$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 9.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=x^2-6x-2$, what is $f(5)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-7$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(5)=1(5)^2-6(5)-2=-7$ Therefore, the verified correct option is -7.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: An exponential growth model is defined by $f(x) = 171 \cdot 2^{x/9}$. What is the value $f(18)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $87$. Evaluating at $x = 18$ gives $171 \cdot 2^2 = 684$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 56. What is the smaller integer?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $7$. $n(n+1)=56 \implies n^2+n-56=0 \implies (n-7)(n+8)=0 \implies n=7$

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: The graph shows $f(x) = -x^2 + 4$. What is the maximum value of $f$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $4$. The vertex of $f(x)=-x^2+4$ is at $(0,4)$, which is the maximum value.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the larger of the two solutions to $x^2-4x-32=0$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $8$. Factor: $(x+4)(x-8)=0 \Rightarrow x=-4 \text{ or } x=8$. Larger $=8$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^2+2x-2$, what is $f(5)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $58$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(5)=2(5)^2+2(5)-2=58$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 58.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.answer: **Answer:** $63$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(-4)=4(-4)^2+2(-4)+7=63$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 63.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: The parabola $y=x^2-8x+15$ intersects the $x$-axis at $x=3$ and $x=5$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $4$. Vertex is midway: $x=\frac{3+5}{2}=4$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: For what sum of $x$-values does the graph of $y=x^2-3x-10$ cross the $x$-axis?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3$. The $x$-intercepts are $x=-2$ and $x=5$ (from factoring), so their sum is $3$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the sum of the solutions to $x^2+5x-36=0$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-5$. By Vieta's formulas, sum of roots $=-\frac{b}{a}=-\frac{5}{1}=-5$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the larger of the two solutions to $x^2+5x+6=0$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $-2$. Factor: $(x+2)(x+3)=0 \Rightarrow x=-2 \text{ or } x=-3$. Larger $=-2$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: Consider the cubic polynomial $f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + 10x - 20$. What is the remainder $f(2)$ upon division by $(x - 2)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3$. By the Remainder Theorem, $f(2) = 2^3 - 5(2^2) + 10(2) - 20 = -12$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: The quadratic function $f(x) = -x^2 + 12x - 18$ attains its maximum at $x = g$. What is the maximum value $f(g)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $107$. The vertex occurs at $g = 6$, giving $f(6) = 36 - 18 = 18$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=x^2-5x+5$, what is $f(-4)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $41$. Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(-4)=1(-4)^2-5(-4)+5=41$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 41.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $x^2 + 6x + 9 = 25$, what is a possible value of $x + 3$?

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: In the partial fraction identity $\frac{6}{(x - 11)(x - 13)} = \frac{f}{x - 13} - \frac{g}{x - 11}$, $f$ and $g$ are constants. What is the sum $f + g$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2$. Matching numerators gives $f = 3$ and $g = 3$, so $f + g = 6$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Fluency (21–28)

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: Which value of $x$ satisfies $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$?
questions.answer: $(x-2)(x-3)=0 \Rightarrow x=2$ or $x=3$. Choice: $x=2$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the vertex of the parabola $y=-2x^2-32x-136$?

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: How many $x$-intercepts does the graph of $y=2x^2+2x$ have?
questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(2)^2-4(2)(0)=4$, which is positive, giving two real intercept(s).

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: How many $x$-intercepts does the graph of $y=2x^2+6x$ have?
questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(6)^2-4(2)(0)=36$, which is positive, giving two real intercept(s).

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the vertex of the parabola $y=x^2-8x+21$?
questions.answer: Vertex $x=-\frac{b}{2a}=4$, $y=f(4)=5$. Vertex $=(4,5)$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: How many $x$-intercepts does the graph of $y=x^2-2x+4$ have?
questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(-2)^2-4(1)(4)=-12$, which is negative, giving zero real intercept(s).

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: How many $x$-intercepts does the graph of $y=-x^2+4x-4$ have?
questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(4)^2-4(-1)(-4)=0$, which is zero, giving one real intercept(s).

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: How many $x$-intercepts does the graph of $y=-x^2+5x-1$ have?
questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(5)^2-4(-1)(-1)=21$, which is positive, giving two real intercept(s).

questions.answer: $(x-2)(x-3)=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \text{ or } x=3$.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=4x^2+7x$, what is $f(5)$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(5)=4(5)^2+7(5)=135$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 135.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=5x^2+3$, what is $f(4)$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(4)=5(4)^2(4)+3=83$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 83.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the vertex of the parabola $y=-3x^2-6x+5$?

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=4x^2-x+9$, what is $f(1)$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(1)=4(1)^2-1(1)+9=12$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 12.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: If $f(x)=3x^2-x+7$, what is $f(-5)$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $f(-5)=3(-5)^2-1(-5)+7=87$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 87.

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola given by $y = 3x^2 - 7x + 12$?
questions.answer: Evaluate at $x = 0$: $y = 3(0)^2 - 7(0) + 12 = 12$. The y-intercept is $(0, 12)$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.target: Quadratic Equations, Vertex Form, Discriminant & Parabolas
questions.q: Which is equivalent to $(x+4)^2-9$?
questions.answer: Applying Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations principles, $x^2+8x+16-9=x^2+8x+7$. Therefore, the verified correct option is $x^2+8x+7$.

questions.answer: Vertex $x=-\frac{b}{2a}=7$, $y=f(7)=4$. Vertex $=(7,4)$.

questions.answer: Discriminant $=b^2-4ac=(-1)^2-4(-1)(2)=9$, which is positive, giving two real intercept(s).
